$about: 2026-08-06, seventh round of the day: the two severe spec-vs-decision-record findings. Both were first re-verified against the current tree (the documented procedure, by grep), then the fix was tested the only way prose can be - paired dry runs of one product-owner request against copies of the test-greenfield-core fixture, pre-fix and post-fix, each agent told to follow the repo's documented procedure literally and to say which of its reads the procedure instructed and which were its own initiative. The fixture itself was not modified; the runs used copies with the patched skills installed. The post-fix run found two holes in the fix and both were closed before this was recorded.

$elicitation.$why: This corpus measures whether the tooling conforms - gates, manifests, drift counts. No person was prompted in any of these runs and none was meant to be, so it evidences nothing about whether the standard asks anybody anything. It was never labelled that way, which is how 377 green observations came to read as validation of a product whose central promise is being guided.

observations.evidence: Reproduced first: `grep -c -i retired` over every standard/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md returned 2 for spec-update, spec-impact and discovery-digest, 1 for spec-reconcile, and 0 for spec-specify - unchanged from the 2026-08-04 finding. spec-specify's only instruction for an existing capability was 'If specs/<short-name>/ already exists, this is the same capability: update the existing spec in place', matching on the slug it had just invented and reading no Status. Now: it lists specs/ and matches on subject before anything else (the fixture's own case - a request for shift reminders generates `shift-reminders`, while the capability is `shift-notifications`, so slug matching finds nothing and mints a rival spec), then reads the matched spec's Status, and `retired` stops it before drafting, names the record and hands the call back to the user rather than either editing the retired spec or minting a fresh directory unasked. Verified by dry run rather than by inspection: an agent given the PO request 'People keep missing their shifts. I want us to start reminding them before a shift starts again - and this time let each person choose whether they get a push notification or an SMS', told to follow the repo's documented procedure literally, stopped at BDR-004 and reported 'The stop is entirely inside the documented procedure, not my own initiative.' The pre-fix control run on the same request also stopped - but attributed it to specs/constitution.md's hard stop plus its own decision to chase the pointer, stating that spec-specify's text 'never mentions decision records at all'; the constitution is loaded at specify step 4, after step 2 has already chosen the directory, so that route is late by construction and depends on an agent volunteering. Residual, stated rather than hidden: this is prose an agent can skip, evidenced by one run of one agent on one fixture.

Reproduced first: grepping standard/.claude/skills/spec-specify/SKILL.md and spec-clarify/SKILL.md for decision-record paths returned only the PATCHED provenance comments naming ADR-002/010/024 - neither skill read docs/decision-records/, and both named docs/discovery/ as the pre-user answer source, which ADR-024 makes explicitly non-normative. standard/AGENTS.md's red flag 2 read 'Contradicting an Accepted ADR', naming one stream. Now: both skills read the decision-record index before drafting or asking, open in full only the records whose subject overlaps, and treat an Accepted record as the answer rather than a question; clarify excludes record-settled items when building its question queue and refuses an answer that contradicts a record, routing it to adr-write/bdr-write as the supersession it is. AGENTS.md's red flag and specs/constitution.template.md's hard stop now name both streams; R6 states the binding half the suite was already citing it for. Verified by dry run: reading docs/decision-records/ was the agent's first substantive action and it cited the step that told it to. That run also broke the first draft of this fix in two ways, both now closed - the fixture's bdr/README.md index stops at BDR-003 while BDR-004 is on disk, so an index-bounded read would have missed exactly the governing record (the skills now say the bound rests on decision-records-check and to list the directory where that guard is not running, and the agent grepped the fixture's CI, found no guard, listed the directory and found BDR-004); and the retirement clause as first written forbade minting a differently-named directory outright, contradicting BDR-004's own text that a future need is a new capability specced fresh.
